attributes.body_ja:
「かのようだ」は、(A) のように「見（み）える・感（かん）じられる」ものの、実際（じっさい）にはそうでない、または確信（かくしん）が持（も）てない、というときに使（つか）われる定型（ていけい）表現（ひょうげん）です。これは副助詞（ふくじょし）「か」と「の」、そして助動詞（じょどうし）「ようだ」の組（く）み合（あ）わせでできています。「か」が付（つ）くことで、「ようだ」だけを使（つか）う場合（ばあい）よりも、より不確（ふたし）かなニュアンスが強調（きょうちょう）されています。

「かのようだ」は、動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、または「である」を伴（ともなう）うナ形容詞（けいようし）または名詞（めいし）に続（つづ）いて使（つか）われます。

「ようだ」が動詞（どうし）や名詞（めいし）を修飾（しゅうしょく）する場合（ばあい）は、「ように」や「ような」と形（かたち）が変（か）わります。

この文型（ぶんけい）は「まるで」のような例（たと）えを表（あらわ）す表現（ひょうげん）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われることがよくあり、この場合（ばあい）、比喩的（ひゆてき）なニュアンスがより強（つよ）まります。
attributes.body:
かのようだ is a set phrase in Japanese indicating that something 'appears to be (A)', but the speaker is not certain. It will be translated as 'as if (A)', or 'just like (A)'. This is a combination of the adverbial particle か, の and the auxiliary verb 様（よう）だ 'appearing to be'. The more literal meaning can be thought of as 'is it not like (A)?', due to the uncertainty expressed by か.

かのようだ may follow verbs and い-Adjectives, or な-Adjectives and nouns followed by である.

When ようだ is altering the meaning of a verb or a noun later in the sentence, ように or ような may also be used.

This grammar construction will often be seen with expressions that emphasize the speaker's assumption about (A), such as まるで. If compared to English, this merely strengthens the sentence in a similar way to the difference between 'it's as if (A)', and 'it's just as if (A)'.

attributes.description: All uses of volitional form and よう explained

attributes.body: Both ようだ and かのようだ express appearance or resemblance, but with different nuance. ようだ means 'It seems' or 'It appears,' and can be used whether the speaker believes the thing is actually as it appears or not. かのようだ adds a stronger, often figurative tone like 'just as if (A)', and is typically used when the speaker knows it is it not actually that thing.

second_relatable.title: ようだ
second_relatable.meaning: It seems that, It appears that, It looks like

attributes.body: Both express resemblance, but with different nuance. かのようだ is used at sentence-end to compare to a hypothetical or exaggerated situation, as in 夢かのようだ (It’s like a dream). ふうに is more neutral and connective, describing manner or appearance, as in こんなふうに書く (Write it like this).

second_relatable.title: ふうに
second_relatable.meaning: ~ way, In a way that suggests, Like ~

attributes.body: Both describe how something appears, but differ in tone. かのようだ often conveys imagination or unreality, as in 幻かのようだ (It’s like an illusion). という風に shows how something visibly seems, as in 分かっているというふうに笑った (He smiled as if he knew).

second_relatable.title: という風に
second_relatable.meaning: As if to say, As if to suggest that, In such a way that, Things like

attributes.body: These are minor variations of the same basic expression meaning 'as if it were (A)'. まるで adds an emphatic nuance, implying it's 'just like' the thing it's being compared to, e.g. まるで夢のようだ 'It's just like a dream.' If the question particle か is present, it adds a nuance of uncertainty, highlighting that though it seems like that thing, the speaker doubts it is (or knows it is not) that thing, e.g. 日本にいるかのようだ 'It's like I'm in Japan (though I'm not).'

first_relatable.title: まるで…ようだ
first_relatable.meaning: It is entirely as if, It is just as though

attributes.body: かのようだ and ように・ような both use よう, meaning 'seems', but have different specific uses. かのようだ carries a strong hypothetical nuance and is often used to mean 'just like' or 'as if' when comparing to obviously different things. In contrast, ように・ような expresses comparison in a more direct or neutral way and can be used whether the similarity is hypothetical or real.
